name: Bismuth oxychloride

lead: Bismuth oxychloride (BiOCl) is a layered mineral crystal that reflects light with a pearly sheen. In cosmetics it appears as the pigment CI 77163 in powders, eye shadows, nail polish and hair sprays, where it makes skin look luminous and slightly smoothed.
Its payoff is a glowing, soft-focus finish; because its crystals are layered and soft, powders glide on easily. It has been used in cosmetics since ancient Egypt as "pearl white".

paras: People encounter it as an ingredient in mineral foundation, setting powder, highlighter and eye shadow. It is applied as part of those products rather than on its own.

Hazard classifications list skin, eye and respiratory irritation for the pure substance. Some makeup users on forums report itching from bismuth oxychloride on sensitive or acne-prone skin, while others use it without issues.

angle.text: Bismuth oxychloride gives powders and mineral makeup a luminous, silky finish and helps them glide on skin. People choose products containing it for a glowing look.

lead: Bismuth oxychloride (BiOCl) is an inorganic compound that forms lustrous white crystals with a layered tetragonal structure. The layering gives it a pearly sheen and low hardness. [1]

In cosmetics it is the colorant CI 77163, used as a pearlescent pigment in eye shadow, powders, hair spray and nail polish. It has been used since ancient Egypt, where it was known as "pearl white". [1]

The pure substance carries GHS hazard statements for skin, eye and respiratory irritation. Most research on BiOCl outside cosmetics concerns materials science, such as wastewater treatment and batteries. [1][2]

paras: BiOCl forms layers of chloride, bismuth and oxide ions, which accounts for its pearly sheen and low hardness. It forms when bismuth trichloride hydrolyzes in water. [1]
It is used as a pearlescent pigment in powders, eye shadow, hair sprays and nail polish. [1]

Under GHS the substance carries "Warning" statements for skin, eye and respiratory irritation. [1] A review on bismuth exposure discusses kidney toxicity concerns for bismuth compounds more broadly. [3]
No studies found on cosmetic use. BiOCl has been studied as a material for pollutant removal in wastewater [2] and as a component in experimental cancer therapies and imaging agents. [4]
